See it in everyday life

Built to hold, not to carry

A wearable lower-body and back-support exoskeleton for people with weak legs, weak hands and a slightly bent back. It is a guardian frame that bends with the body, and it goes on over normal clothes in about two minutes.

Back spine bar

550 mm adjustable aluminium 6061 bar supports a bent back without forcing it straight.

Waist belt

Padded belt moves the load onto the hips.

Hip and thigh

0 to 90° hip hinge with a lock pin, plus an adjustable thigh bar and padded cuff.

Knee joint

The core joint: a 30 Nm motor, a spring and a mechanical lock working together.

Ankle and foot

A flexible leaf-spring plate gives push-off. A non-slip 240 mm plate fits inside a sandal.

Hand support

Wrist cuffs and grip support on both hands for rails and balance.

Three layers, one guardian

Mechanics hold the body, electronics sense it, and software decides what the frame does next.

Mechanical structure

Steel and aluminium frame, spring-assisted knee, hip hinge, ankle leaf spring and padded neoprene cuffs.

Electronics and control

ESP32 controller, MPU6050 motion sensor, foot force sensors, geared knee motors, a 12 V Li-ion battery, wrist buttons, buzzer, LED and an emergency cut-off.

Software logic

Seven modes: walk, stair up, stair down, sit, stand, rest and anti-fall, all with slow, speed-limited motor moves.

Load and runtime simulator

Set the wearer and the task. The model estimates knee torque, motor load and battery life against the V1 specifications.

Knee motor load

Estimated runtime

A first-order, quasi-static estimate that assumes the knee spring carries 30% of the load. It is not a clinical or engineering sign-off.

Safe even when the battery is not

Safety is mechanical first, electronic second.

Mechanical lock

If the battery dies, the knee lock still holds and a manual pin is available.

Anti-fall

Sudden tilt past 25° locks both knees in under 0.3 seconds with a buzzer alert.

Slow motors

Motor speed is capped at 30° per second with a gentle ramp.

Natural posture

The sensor zero is the wearer’s own standing posture, never a forced straight back.

The Seva Sentinel Exo is an assistive concept prototype, not a medical cure. Use it only after review by a doctor or physiotherapist.

Built in Jharkhand, for Bharat.
Developed by MVA Robotics Innovation Org., Jharkhand Rai University, Ranchi.
